plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/24686
Template Malware-ext-ransomware-breach. Ransomware per AP; ransom demand documented, so social Extortion added (target/vector Unknown; the demand was shown on hospital computers). Actor named as BYOD extortion group by the attackers themselves; Organized crime / Financial.
Data theft is attacker-claimed only (student, employee, patient PII incl. SSNs, research, HR/payroll, EHR) and UNM HSC said core systems were not penetrated, so data_disclosure Potentially; data varieties coded from the attacker's claim. data_abuse not coded.
NAICS: body's 611110 is wrong; coded 611310 (university) per the NAICS 61 label; the hospital is part of HSC. Government NA (public university, coded like other universities). Discovery: detected internally 11:30 a.m. Monday Oct 26 (method not stated) -> internal Unknown. Assets: U - Desktop or laptop (end-user devices per UNM) and S - Unknown. Employee count 10001 to 25000 (UNM Health system is a large employer) is approximate.

summary: The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center suffered a cyberattack on October 26, 2026 that forced UNM Hospital to divert ambulances, close clinics and cancel appointments and classes for at least two days. Employees saw messages, including a synthetic voice message played on hospital computers, from attackers claiming to be the BYOD extortion group, who said they had stolen student, employee and patient data (SSNs, research data, Oracle databases, HR/payroll records and EHR information) and demanded a ransom. UNM HSC said the incident affected end-user devices but did not penetrate core systems. AP described it as a ransomware attack; the FBI is investigating.
